reviews.comment: Hartell may not be an above and beyond prof but she is fine. Only homework is group projects which are fine and quizzes which are open note. I didn't need to go to class much because she basically just goes over the posted slides, but she almost always has extra credit on Fridays. Tests are easy if you study the "Learning Concepts" for each unit.

Hartell is a really nice woman and explained things well in her lectures. The exams are tough though, so just be sure to study off of the learning objectives. The group projects are really fun but make sure you get a solid group to work with.

I say class isn't mandatory, but on random days (mostly Fridays) she gives extra credit just for showing up. I just went to class to play games, in case she gave extra credit. Quizzes are open note, and like 80% of the tests are exact quiz questions. If you study the quiz answers, and have a basic understanding of content in lecture, it's an easy A

Took in Fall 2025. Attendance was mostly not required except for a few group project days. The class was manageable overall, but it is very test-heavy, which can make it challenging depending on your test-taking style. Outside of exams, assignments were relatively easy and the material was interesting.
Get a good group for the group projects

Dr. Hartell is a great professor. She explains what is going to be on the test very clearly. While the class has 3 exams and a final there are plenty of easy group assignments to balance out the tests. Also the tests are not to difficult. I really only lightly studied 2 days prior and got Bs on all my tests.
She is very good, everything she has on the learning objectives on the slides will be on the test. There are no surprises, if you do bad it's because you didn't study and learn simple as that

Super nice, no attendance mandatory. Tests are super hard and lots of visual memorization, all slides provided. You must study if you want to do well. Lots of extra credit given, but no rounding up grades (but she's very clear about that from the start of class). Class is all group work, so if you have a bad group it can be really hard.

I dont understand why her rating is so low. Most complaints are about her not rounding up, but she is very clear about that on the first day of class. If you show up, you will do fine in this class. It is extremely easy and she makes sure you know what is expected of you. She is a good professor and I would have no problem taking her again.
ended with a 79.7 and she did not round up the grade, you should show up to every class

She was definitely not the worst professor. Personally, I feel like she is mainly here to do her own research. The class was an 8 am, but not mandatory, but if you chose to go to class, a lot of extra credit was given. The test and quiz materials can all be found in the slides given to you, so only go to class if you really need E.C. (worth it).

Worst Prof I have ever had at TAMU. Have taken both of the courses she teaches, BAD BOTH TIMES. She cancels classes every week making it impossible to learn the material needed. Almost everyone has an A in the class until the final exam which the average was in the 50s and no curve. OTHER PROFS in the department have told me she's awful at teaching
Good professor overall. As long as you show up to lectures and pay attention you will do great on the tests. Also show up to Friday classes as she gives out bonus points on Fridays.

The labs are hard because they're so time consuming and most COSC majors can't do complex math. Julie is a person that's all over the place. She's funny yet when it comes to teaching, she's not the best. Mediocre at most.  Her grading is lenient and relaxed. A lot of teamwork in the labs so be prepared to backpack your lab-mates.

This is the worst teacher I have ever had. She only shows up to the 50 minute lecture and never to the labs. She will go over the most basic things in class with no instruction on how to do the lab and expect us to fully understand how to execute the lab. Everything she says contradicts the book. Quizzes are over things never discussed.
